title: Opioid use disorder evidence page
summary: Evidence level: early human and observational. Human evidence: Observational detoxification reports, follow-up studies, and registered oral Ibogaine withdrawal research. Main limitation: Durability, relapse denominator data, missing follow-up, concurrent supports, and adverse-event denominator data remain incomplete. Safety: Cardiac risk, concurrent substances, withdrawal physiology, electrolyte issues, psychiatric status, and medication interactions. Not proven: Ibogaine is not proven to cure opioid addiction.

title: Alcohol use disorder evidence page
summary: Evidence level: very limited. Human evidence: FDA allowed an early phase U.S. Noribogaine hydrochloride study to proceed after an IND submission in April 2026. Main limitation: Noribogaine, Ibogaine, plant Iboga, alcohol-withdrawal risk, and clinic claims are separate subjects. Safety: Alcohol withdrawal, liver health, medications, QT/QTc, electrolytes, and monitoring requirements. Not proven: Noribogaine is not FDA-approved for alcohol use disorder.

title: Traumatic brain injury evidence page
summary: Evidence level: limited observational. Human evidence: A 30-person veteran prospective observational study and later neurophysiology work drew attention and require side-by-side design-limit explanation. Main limitation: Small sample, male veteran population, Mexico treatment setting, concurrent supports, selection effects, and short follow-up. Safety: Screening, cardiac monitoring, magnesium context, psychiatric history, and follow-up. Not proven: Ibogaine is not proven as a general TBI treatment.

title: PTSD and trauma symptoms evidence page
summary: Evidence level: limited observational. Human evidence: PTSD-related signals often appear within veteran or substance-use populations rather than standalone PTSD trials. Main limitation: Confounding, expectation effects, integration/support differences, psychiatric exclusions, and concurrent interventions. Safety: Psychiatric destabilization, suicidality screening, medications, acute monitoring, and post-session support. Not proven: Ibogaine is not proven as a PTSD treatment.

title: Depression and mood symptoms evidence page
summary: Evidence level: very limited. Human evidence: Mood improvements appear in some Ibogaine-related observational and veteran studies, usually as secondary outcomes. Main limitation: Expectation effects, concurrent treatment, post-acute recovery, integration, and regression to the mean can affect mood measures. Safety: Suicidality, bipolar disorder, psychosis risk, serotonergic medications, sleep disruption, and cardiac risk. Not proven: Ibogaine is not proven as a depression treatment.

title: Anxiety symptoms evidence page
summary: Evidence level: secondary outcomes. Human evidence: Anxiety outcomes are usually measured within TBI, PTSD, or substance-use populations rather than as a standalone indication. Main limitation: Anxiety can change with withdrawal relief, sleep, expectation, setting, or integration support. Safety: Acute distress, panic, psychiatric destabilization, benzodiazepines, serotonergic drugs, and cardiac monitoring. Not proven: Ibogaine is not proven as an anxiety treatment.

title: Parkinson's disease evidence page
summary: Evidence level: no direct human data. Human evidence: A 2026 peer-reviewed case report describes one patient treated with low-dose Ibogaine hydrochloride over 80 days using validated Parkinson's instruments. Main limitation: One-patient evidence is highly uncertain and vulnerable to placebo, expectation, medication changes, and disease variability. Safety: Age, cardiac status, neurological comorbidity, drug interactions, sleep worsening, and medication changes. Not proven: Ibogaine is not proven as a Parkinson's treatment.

title: Withdrawal and cravings evidence page
summary: Evidence level: limited observational. Human evidence: Withdrawal and craving findings appear in OUD studies, observational detoxification reports, and substance-use reviews. Main limitation: Concurrent medications, setting, expectation, follow-up loss, and substance-specific withdrawal risks can change interpretation. Safety: Withdrawal physiology, dehydration, electrolytes, cardiac risk, benzodiazepines, alcohol, stimulants, opioids, and polysubstance use. Not proven: Craving reduction or withdrawal relief is not the same as a cure.

title: Howard Lotsof and the 1962 Ibogaine observation
summary: Howard Lotsof reported in 1962 that Ibogaine unexpectedly interrupted heroin withdrawal and craving. The story is foundational to modern Western Ibogaine addiction-treatment interest, but it is history and advocacy context, not proof of cure or safety.

title: Claim check: Ibogaine cures addiction
